Mrs. Vale's mathematics class has 26 students, each with unique two initials. Since each student's first and last name begin with the same letter, their initials must be pairs of the same letter (AA, BB, ..., ZZ). This means there are 26 unique initials corresponding to each letter from A to Z.

The problem states that the letter "Y" is considered a vowel, so the vowels are A, E, I, O, U, and Y, totaling 6 vowels. Each of these vowels corresponds to a student with those initials (AA, EE, II, OO, UU, YY), resulting in 6 students with vowel initials.

The probability of randomly picking a student with vowel initials is the number of vowel-initial students divided by the total number of students. This fraction is \(\frac{6}{26}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{3}{13}\).
